Subject: PoC recap & proposed next steps (deployment mode options)

Hi Claire / Jose —

Thanks again for the demo today — really appreciated the context on your user flows and the regulatory constraints for PII in EU-region accounts. Quick recap and a proposed PoC path so we can get alignment on deployment mode (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC/on-prem) and timelines.

Call recap (high level):
- Primary goal: reduce inference latency and cost for your chat assistant while ensuring customer data never leaves Acme's VPC.
- Key constraints: data residency (EU), SOC2/ISO compliance, and a preference for tenant isolation.
- Stakeholders: Claire (product), Jose (security), infra lead TBD (you mentioned an infra owner).

Recommended PoC options to evaluate (we can do one or run parallel tracks):
1) Hosted API (fastest) — Redwood hosted, quick onboarding, good for functional validation. Not ideal for your data residency requirement.
2) Dedicated capacity — reserved pool for Acme in our EU region. Offers strong performance and data isolation at the compute level, data still flows through Redwood-managed infra.
3) Private VPC / on-prem — customer-managed network (VPC peering or on-prem appliance). Best for strict residency and audit controls; longer setup.

Proposed PoC plan (preferred starting point: Private VPC trial given your constraints):
- Timeline: 4 weeks (kickoff, setup, validation, wrap-up).
- Success criteria: p95 latency <200ms for 1k concurrent sessions, end-to-end request processing with KV caching enabled, automated audit log delivery, and SOC2 checklist items validated.
- Stakeholders to commit: product, security, infra, and a single technical lead from Acme for networking.

Attachments: PoC-scope.pdf (scope + milestone checklist).

Can you confirm (1) which deployment mode you want to prioritize, (2) who the infra contact is, and (3) whether a Private VPC trial is acceptable as the primary path? If you prefer Dedicated first, we can scope that too and give rough pricing.

If helpful, I can draft a mutual action plan and share a proposed kickoff slot — available Wed/Thu next week.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Hi all —

Quick tech follow-ups from the infra/solutions side so we can size the Private VPC trial properly:

1) Expected QPS / peak concurrent sessions (approx)? You mentioned 1k concurrent in the doc — is that peak or steady?
2) Typical sequence length (average tokens per request) and any long context requirements?
3) Will you be sending raw user data to the model or pre-filtered/hashed tokens? We need to know whether full PII will transit the link.
4) For audit logs: do you prefer S3 delivery, syslog, or direct SIEM push?

For Private VPC options: we can do VPC peering to an EU-region dedicated cluster (fastest) or an on-prem appliance if you require air-gapped operation (longer lead time). The peering path supports KV cache and autoscaling policies similar to Dedicated.

If you can send answers to the above, we can prepare a tailored PoC plan and a rough cost delta between Dedicated and Private runs.

Thanks,
Rishi
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks Claire / Jose — this is helpful. Per Rishi's asks, I've sketched a concrete PoC timeline and deliverables. See bullets below and the attached proposed-poc-plan.xlsx (milestones + owner matrix).

Proposed 4-week PoC (Private VPC preferred):
Week 0 (kickoff): finalize network details, exchange firewall/IP allowlist, sign trial agreement (DocuSign).
Week 1 (setup): VPC peering & routing, initial deployment of model variant in EU cluster, connectivity tests.
Week 2 (validation): run synthetic load tests, validate KV cache performance, deliver logs to Acme SIEM.
Week 3 (user tests & wrap): run customer flows, collect latency/cost metrics, capture audit evidence for SOC2 items.

Success criteria (must pass all):
- End-to-end p95 latency <200ms for target workload during synthetic test
- KV cache hit rate >= 60% for repeated prompts where applicable
- Audit logs delivered and parsable by Acme SIEM
- No data exfiltration; validated network flow logs show only allowed endpoints

Operational asks from Acme:
- Provide infra lead and firewall owner for allowlisting (Priya ideally).
- Approve DocuSign trial agreement so we can start Week 0.

I've created a HubSpot deal and attached the proposed plan: https://hubspot.example.com/deals/DEAL-2026-ACME-01
DocuSign trial link: https://docusign.example.com/txn/XYZ123

Attachments: proposed-poc-plan.xlsx

Let me know which kickoff dates work — I'm proposing Wed 11 Mar or Thu 12 Mar (EU-friendly times ok).

Best,
Marissa
